commits.body:
The merge loop checked step 1 of the reconcile before merging anything. Every stream loop has stopped, and the verification queue is empty, but only the values stream's brief ends blocked. Objects, environment and reuse still end 'Status: working': each session stopped without setting a status, and run-streams.sh counts a clean stop with no status as done, which the brief's reconcile does not accept ('not only an inactive scope'). Each has work of its own left: objects records its passed O2 job and waits on the merge and on a decision about O3's frozen allocation bound; environment is blocked on the objects and values streams by its own account; reuse reads job 20261108-063259's figures into R3. The brief's Progress records this and ends blocked, with what the user can do: set the status back to working and rerun run-streams.sh (which reruns only the three, then this loop), or count them finished and let the merge take what they committed. Verified by reading each stream's @- brief, the loop summaries, the systemd scopes and the pipeline status; no code changed.

commits.summary: Loops record why they stop: a stop that leaves a brief's status working gets a turn to set it, and run-streams.sh no longer counts it as done
commits.body:
On 2026-11-08 three application-core streams (objects, environment, reuse) ended with their briefs still at 'Status: working'. Each session decided 'LOOP: stop' in feature-loop.sh's decision turn and wrote the status it meant there ('waiting on jobs ...', 'blocked: ...'), but that turn may not edit or commit, and the cycle before it was never asked to keep the status line current. feature-loop.sh then exited 0, and run-streams.sh counted a clean stop with no status as done, so objects and reuse were never rerun when their jobs came back, and the merge loop refused the reconcile.

feature-loop.sh: the cycle instruction now asks the session to keep a brief's '- Status:' line current in each commit; the decision turn is told a status is never its last line; and when the session decides to stop while the status still says working, one more turn before the compact sets the status the brief's Loop until gives and commits it. If that leaves the status working or uncommitted, the loop ends with exit 1, as needing attention. run-streams.sh: a clean stop whose status is neither done, blocked nor waiting on jobs is now run once more, like a failure, and counts as blocked the second time.

Verified with bash -n on both scripts and a stubbed test of brief_status, has_status and close_status: a stop with status working that the session fixes and commits (ok), one it leaves alone (failed), one edited but not committed (failed), an already blocked status and a brief with no status line (no turn). The stream workspaces run their own copy of feature-loop.sh, so the same file is committed in each before the rerun.

commits.summary: feature-loop.sh finds a brief in its own workspace first, so a stream reads and is pointed at its own copy
commits.body:
run-streams.sh starts each stream's copy of feature-loop.sh with the default workspace as its current directory, and feature-loop.sh looked a relative brief up from there first. Every stream therefore ran with the default workspace's copy of its brief: the cycle instruction pointed the session at it, the brief-changed check hashed it, and since kppsnzyn close_status read its status from it. No stream edits that copy, so its Progress is the launch-time one. In this morning's rerun the objects and environment sessions set their status in their own copies; close_status read 'working' in the default copy, asked for an extra turn, and ended the loops as needing attention, with exit 1. run-streams.sh reads each stream's own copy, so both still came out blocked. The objects session diagnosed this in its run summary.

A relative brief is now looked up under the script's own repo first and then from the caller's directory, and named relative to the repo as before. Verified by running the resolution with the objects workspace as the root and the default workspace as the current directory (it gives the workspace's own llm-dlc/loops/application-core-objects.md), with the default workspace as the root, and with an absolute path. The file was replaced by rename, since run-streams.sh is running. The reuse stream, still running, keeps the old behaviour until it stops, and the stream workspaces' copies get this change at the merge.

commits.summary: application-core objects O3: the frozen throttle claims bound allocations at 1, the user's decision, so the contract's O3 passes
commits.body:
The frozen throttle claims (throttle-constructed-claim, throttle-setup-claim) said allocations 0 in both versions, but Throttle#allows makes the IllegalArgumentException it throws for negative units. The domain gate counts every allocation on any path, so the contract's O3 came out unresolved instead of expected.json's verdicts. Phase 0 already counted such a throw in checked-claim (bound 1), so the user decided the 0 was a slip: both claims are now bounded at 1 in each version, and expected.json is unchanged. The user also decided that the bound covers the target call only: setup calls are bounded by the plan's setup_calls and their outcomes are compared, so their allocations aren't counted, and the gate stays as it is.

The stream's test helper throttle_claim, which raised the bound to 1 to work around the fixture, now asserts it instead. Verified inline: tests/application_core.rs 14 of 14 (13 before, O3 failing), tests/application_core_objects.rs 21 passed and 1 ignored (the cache test that waits on the reuse stream, as before). The brief's Progress records the decision, and the status is blocked only on O2's String adapter, which waits for the merge. Made by the user's session from the default workspace while this stream's loop was stopped.

commits.summary: application-core reuse R3 done: the shared JDK image table's release figures, read from job 20261108-063259
commits.body:
Job 20261108-063259 (passed at 3841df5e, 3m22s, peak 1.7 GiB) ran the same release benchmark as job 20261108-060410, with the JDK image's table of classes now shared within the process. It reached the same verdicts in all four scenarios, both in process and as a process. Medians of 7, before the cache and with it: an unchanged rerun took 209.8 ms and now 8.6 ms in process (290.3 and 66.1 ms as a process), the cold run 460.6 and 65.6 ms, the defect's cold run 2217 and 1576 ms (solving 1723 and 1484 ms), and its rerun 265.3 and 31.9 ms. An open that builds the table takes 7.89 ms, and one that shares it 0.06 ms. javac still takes about 0.4 s per build, so compilation outweighs a whole rerun: the cut is to preparation, not to proving a change. The runner committed the reports (lib/benchmark/preparation/shared-image.*) in the default workspace, and they reach this branch at the merge.

R3's record in the brief's Progress now holds these figures, and lib/README.md's paragraph on preparation gives them in place of the pending note. Verified by reading both jobs' reports in full and comparing their verdicts. Nothing else changed: the README edit is prose only. Also found: the benchmark lacks the acceptance contract's unrelated edit and safe helper rewrite. Without the helper rewrite, it can't show helper evidence apart from exact hits, as the brief's Acceptance asks. Adding them is next, so that J4 at the merge runs the full set.

commits.summary: application-core reuse J4: the cost report's figures with all five cases, read from job 20261108-114325; the stream is done
commits.body:
Job 20261108-114325 (passed at 283aa75d, 3m37s, peak 1.7 GiB) ran lib/tests/preparation.rs in release with the acceptance contract's five cases on the joint example: cold, an unchanged rerun, an unrelated edit, a safe rewrite of the helper Pricing.discount, and the offset defect cold and rerun. Every repeat and the process reached the expected verdicts, and every assertion held. Medians of 7, as a process: cold 127.0 ms, rerun 62.5, unrelated edit 64.4 (5 exact hits), helper rewrite 138.7 (1 exact hit, 4 proved: total on the helper's new proof, named by key, and the route again because its effect proof's closure holds the helper's body), defect cold 1687.6 (1364 ms solving) and its rerun 83.7. The edited build's javac, about 400 ms, is 74-87% of every scenario with compilation except the defect's cold run. So the gain is to a rerun's preparation, not a whole build's, and helper evidence is reused by key, not made cheaper to obtain. The runner committed the reports (lib/benchmark/preparation/j4.*) in the default workspace; they reach this branch at the merge.

The brief's Progress records the figures, the three kinds of reuse apart, and two items for the main loop's for-review list: effect proofs don't use helper evidence, and the R2 contract row still stops at the objects stream's construction::receiver until the merge. lib/README.md's preparation paragraph gives the two new cases. Verified by reading the job's report, its log and j4.json's verdicts in full; the README change is prose only. The stream's items are done (R1, R2, R3's justified outcome, J3, and J4's report), with R4 left out as the brief allows, so the status is done. J4's rerun on the merged revision is the main loop's Phase 5, and the interface requests recorded under R1 wait for the merge.

commits.summary: Merge the four application-core streams: objects, values, environment and reuse
commits.body:
The reconcile of llm-dlc/loops/application-core.md (Phase 5, step 1). All four streams had finished: objects, values and environment blocked on work only the merge makes possible, and reuse done. No stream loop or integration check was running, and no verification job was pending. Each stream's last turns were recorded on its branch (Record session traces: objects qqywzsvy, values kyqtplry, environment krwlnoop, reuse yxlnwoss), and their 46 logs not yet in the default workspace were copied in. The four branches were then merged with the default line's tvwtmzkx. The workspaces application-core-objects, -values, -environment, -reuse and -integration are forgotten; their directories stay on disk for the user to delete.

Conflicts: only the generated llm-dlc/README.md session table, llm-dlc/index.json, llm-dlc/traces/README.md and llm-dlc/traces/metrics.json. The default line's side was taken, and this commit regenerates them. The files that more than one line changed merged cleanly: lib/README.md (each stream's paragraphs, in places of their own), lib/tests/conformance.rs, and feature-loop.sh and run-streams.sh, where the same stop-status fix was committed on each line.

Verified inline on the merge: the integration check (application-core-integration.sh) passes: the contract lib/tests/application_core.rs 14 of 14, the library's unit tests (254), foundations, compare and effects, and the build.py, review, run-record and performance suites. Every other test binary but integration.rs, whose tests run JBMC, also passes: alignment 34, application_core_objects 21, conformance 10, environment 16, heap 49, observations 12, reuse 11, reuse_summaries 14, skill 1, summaries 40 and values 16 (JBMC tests and two reproducers that wait on interface requests are ignored, as on the branches). So does every Python suite. The contract accepts a stream's named refusal as passing, so it doesn't yet say which rows reach their verdicts; Phase 5's for-review list has to.

The brief's Progress folds the streams' work. The timebox deferred nothing. The interface requests that waited for the merge are listed in order: the String and list parameter wiring that V1, V2 and O2 wait on; values::resolve in the checks; equivalence::confirm's stub rule for VF-023; the cache's roots of a setup sequence; the environment stream's E3 and Q's rows; smaller requests; and the lib/README.md sentences the streams couldn't rewrite. The streams' findings for review are listed too. Next: those requests, one per cycle with its reproducer, then Phase 5's joint acceptance as jobs.

Out of date in the rest of the brief: Where it starts from describes the state before the streams.

commits.summary: application-core Phase 5 step 1: a String parameter of a regression check, so the contract's V1 row reaches its verdicts
commits.body:
The values stream's interface request for V1, applied at the merge. values::adapter now gives the regression check the String adapter (at most --max-array-length code units, never null). equivalence passes the bound to the own checker, reads the witness's String as a new jbmc::Argument::String by the adapter's own rule (values::string_units), rebuilds it for the replay by rebuild's rule (values::new_string), shrinks it, renders it as an escaped Java literal, and also runs it on a JVM as new String(char[]). The statement states a ParameterKind::Value with its bound, Bounds::max_value_length and Models::values, and the regression cache's claim key covers the bound and the String model's identity. JBMC is refused under --engine jbmc and not asked under --confirm, since its Strings are its own model.

Verified inline: the contract's V1 row now accepts no stream's refusal (it failed before) and passes, with Codes#vip's rewrite proved and wrong-prefix refuted on vip("VI"), replayed in the interpreter and on JDK 25.0.5. The new lib/tests/value_parameters.rs has 4 tests: the correct case and the defect, an isolated surrogate crossing to the JVM unit for unit (a sabotage of the JVM's units fails it), the named refusals, and a cached proof reused exactly and proved again under another bound. The integration check passes (contract 14/14, 254 unit tests), as does every other test binary but integration.rs, whose String test now expects the JBMC refusal and was run inline. Still refused by name: a String in a property check, a String result (Objects.equals is a gap), a String plan root, a null String. The list half of the request is next.

commits.summary: application-core Phase 5 step 1: a list parameter of a regression check, so the contract's V2 regressions reach their verdicts
commits.body:
Interface request 1's list half, for plain regression checks. A java.util.List<E> parameter whose generic signature names one element class is now a harness slot of its own (harness::Slot::List), of at most --max-array-length elements, never null. The harness makes that many objects of E by their constructor in each version from the same leaves, and each version's list from the values adapter's int choices in the shape ListAdapter::java writes, skipping what ListAdapter::admitted doesn't admit, so any two elements may be one object. List.of is called through a small branchless class file of version 52 written beside the harness (harness::LISTS_CLASS), since the harness's version 49 can't invokestatic an interface's method. The objects' fields are compared after the calls. The witness stays flat ints and leaves; its list is read by ListAdapter::read, rendered as List.of(new Line(1, 1), the same object as lines[0]), typed as a list of nodes, rebuilt over each version's objects for the interpreter's replay, and run on a JVM. jvm_witness now sizes max_stack from the arguments' widths (part of interface request 6): an eight-line witness failed with 'Stack size too large' before. The statement states the list as a value with its bound and the list model, and the cache key covers the model, the elements' constructors and the helper class. JBMC is not asked (--engine jbmc refused, --confirm not-asked, per VF-023).

The reproducer: the contract's V2 regressions accepted the values stream's refusal and now accept none, under the frozen claims' list bound of 3; they failed before. Verified: the integration check passes (contract 14/14, lib 254, foundations, compare, effects, the Python suites), and so does every other test binary but integration.rs (JBMC). V2's ten regression cases reach expected.json's verdicts, and the defects duplicate-skipped and alias-blind are refuted on witnesses replayed on JDK 25.0.5. tests/value_parameters.rs gains three tests: correct cases and defects with the statement, the named refusals (raw or wildcard lists, elements holding arrays or objects, an object result that could be an element, JBMC, a property's list), and cached evidence that moves with the bound and with an edit of the element's constructor. Two sabotages (the harness ignoring picks, the replay rebuilding distinct elements) fail them. The planned claims' adapted list root is the next cycle. The brief is not out of date here: interface request 1 asked for ListAdapter::java's shape, which the bytecode harness follows.

commits.summary: application-core Phase 5 step 1: a plan's adapted list root and a result's identity with the list's elements, so the contract's V2 claims reach their verdicts
commits.body:
Interface request 1's last part (llm-dlc/loops/application-core.md). construction::check_plans now takes a construction plan's root that is an adapted list of application objects, named as the root. It resolves the root's domain under this tool's list model (values::resolve), and refuses by name a list that may be null, an adapted String root, and roots that differ between the versions. The regression check makes the list as it makes a list parameter, under the domain's own bound (the frozen basket claims' 3) rather than --max-array-length. An object result that the check follows into its fields is no longer refused next to a list: the harness, the replay and the Java text compare it for identity with each of the list's objects, before and now (harness::Root::Element, named lines[0] for the first object and lines.m1, ... for the others). That covers basket-first-claim's identity:result==lines[0]. The statement states the list's objects as one observation of the list, so a claim's field:lines is compared. The list counts among the input objects, and a contract input may name a generic parameter by its erased type.

Verified: the contract (lib/tests/application_core.rs) accepts no refusal for V2's claims any more and passes 14 of 14. basket-total-claim and basket-clear-claim reach all ten of expected.json's verdicts. basket-first-claim reaches four of its five. copied-first is left unresolved by the allocation gate, because the claim bounds allocations at 0 and the defect's copy makes 2 objects (the Line and the IllegalArgumentException its constructor may throw). expected.json says refuted. A frozen fixture's bound conflicts with its expectation, as O3's did, so this goes to the user, with the options in Progress. Until then the contract holds that one case to exactly the gate's outcome. tests/value_parameters.rs has 3 new tests (10 pass): the plan's own bound, and the identity preserved by the rewrite and refuted on copied-first with the bound raised to 2 (witness replayed on a JVM); seven refusals by name; and a planned claim's cache reused exactly but not under another list bound. Two sabotages fail them: identity references without the list's objects, and the replay reading them as null. The integration check passes, and so does every other test binary but integration.rs (JBMC). Docs: lib/README.md.

commits.summary: application-core Phase 5 step 1: a claim's value domains are resolved under this tool's models before its key, and before a modelled call's or a plan node's adapted value is refused
commits.body:
Interface request 2 of the application-core merge. values::resolve_claim resolves every String and list domain a claim carries (a plan's adapted values at its roots, in its nodes and setup calls; a modelled call's adapted response and an object response's plan), and spec::cache::key resolves the claim before digesting it. A claim stated in the frozen claims' words and the same claim stated by the models' identities are now one key; a claim stated under another model, another JDK or a stronger level, or over a domain the adapters refuse, is uncacheable by name instead of keyed. environment::lower and construction::check_plans resolve an adapted result or node value before refusing it, so another model is refused for that; the adapted-result refusal now names what is missing (no stub makes an adapter's value).

Reproducer: tests/values.rs's a_claims_value_domains_are_resolved_before_its_key_and_its_checks, which failed with each of the three call sites taken out. It also checks values::resolve_claim against the test file's reference walk on all eight frozen claims. tests/reuse.rs's every_semantic_part_of_a_plan_or_a_model_changes_the_key expected other keys for a String model stated at the model's own level and a list model that says it leaves out nothing: once resolved, both are the frozen claim (ValueModels::resolve replaces a stated evidence record with the model's own), so the test now asserts their keys are the frozen claim's; a list of Strings and a String model stated as proved are asserted never keyed. Listed for review in the brief's Progress.

commits.summary: application-core Phase 5 step 1: a JBMC refutation through a stub that doesn't reproduce is no verdict under --confirm, VF-023's rule (verification pending)
commits.body:
Interface request 3 of the application-core merge (llm-dlc/loops/application-core.md). VF-023: under --engine auto --confirm the own checker proves listSizes and listChange, and JBMC 6.11.0 refutes them through its stub of java.util.List.size(), with a witness the interpreter replays as holding; the tool reported 'the engines disagree'. equivalence::confirm now treats a JBMC refutation whose witness does not reproduce and whose preflight finds a stub as no verdict, naming the stubs, as it already did for a construct JBMC runs otherwise than the JVM.
